root_cause: The engine's state file is untracked, so on a fresh runner it does not exist and every product was defaulted to the starting price, which reset the whole shop to three dollars every Friday, reverted any price that had been set by hand, and left the engine unable to learn from a run because it started from nothing every time. The hold path also skipped the clamp, so a stored price outside the rule was published and then refused by the command that lists a product for sale, and a product that is held could never move.
evidence: the state file is in .gitignore, the Friday lane runs pricing.py on a fresh checkout, and the catalogue's own price was never read
repro: run pricing.py against a catalogue with a price of five dollars and no state file
fix: the catalogue is the price of record, a hold is clamped like a move is, and the catalogue decides the tier rather than the engine's note
regression_test: audit_selftest.py runs the engine against a catalogue with a price of five dollars and one outside the rule, and checks both
verification: defaulting to the starting price again makes the checks fail

symptom: a corrupt budget crashed the job instead of refusing it
root_cause: The state file's shape was only checked at the top level, so a file holding a months list instead of a table, or a month that was a number instead of a record, or an hour count that was a word, made spent() raise out of check(). The module promises that an unreadable budget refuses the job. The hours and the broken-ness also came from two separate reads of the same file, so a failed read and a successful one could be combined, and the job was approved on zeros from the failed one.
evidence: a state file holding {"months": []} made check() raise an AttributeError, and one holding a non-numeric hour count raised a ValueError
repro: put each of those shapes in data/budget.json and run budget.py check
fix: the shape is checked before it is used, one read answers both questions, and the temporary file has a unique name so two writers cannot swap each other's file into place
regression_test: audit_selftest.py covers the shape of the state file
verification: putting the old check back makes a corrupt file crash again

symptom: the daily lane believed a corrupt budget was a full month
root_cause: The daily lane asked budget.remaining() for the hours left, and remaining() reads a corrupt state as zero spent, so it answered with a whole month while the truth was unknown. The command that answers this question properly, budget.check(), refuses when the hours cannot be read, and the lane did not use it.
evidence: with a corrupt budget file, broken() was true, check() returned 1 and remaining() returned 30.0
repro: corrupt data/budget.json and run the daily lane
fix: the lane asks budget.check(), which refuses when the hours cannot be read
regression_test: the refusal is the answer, not a number
verification: the daily lane asked for a number again

symptom: the daily lane recorded changes that never happened
root_cause: The lane decided whether anything changed by comparing the bytes of the improver's state file before and after. The improver rewrites that file on every path, including the model proposing nothing and the patch being rejected and rolled back, so the bytes always differed and the lane always said a change had been made. It recorded changes that never happened and started the cooldown on days when nothing was done, so the promise that doing nothing is a success never held.
evidence: the improver rewrites its state file on every path, with a fresh timestamp, so the comparison was always true
repro: run the lane and look at whether it says a change was made when the model declined
fix: the lane reads what the improver recorded, and a change means a patch was kept
regression_test: the lane asks for the recorded outcome rather than the file bytes
verification: comparing the bytes again makes every run claim a change

symptom: the daily lane threw away the patch it had tested
root_cause: The lane committed only the four data files, so the improved generator was written into the working tree, tested there and then thrown away with the runner, while the note saying it had been tried was committed. The memory of the attempt survived and the attempt did not, so the same patch was proposed every day and never kept.
evidence: the commit step staged four data files and nothing else, and the patched file was never staged
repro: read the commit step of the daily lane
fix: the patch is staged with the notes, so a patch that passed the suite is kept
regression_test: the lane's own commit step
verification: removing the staging of the changed files leaves the patch on the runner

symptom: the private-data guard was defeated by a shallow checkout
root_cause: The check that looks for a credential which was committed and then deleted reads the whole log, and the runners checked out one commit by default, so in CI it never saw more than the latest commit while it did see the history on a full clone. The lanes that run it were given the whole history. The scan also failed on a full clone over a test fixture that had been removed from the working tree months earlier, so the gate was red for everybody and meaningless.
evidence: the runners use the default shallow checkout, and a full clone found a token-shaped test fixture in the history that is not in the working tree
repro: run check_repo_hygiene.py on a full clone and on a shallow one
fix: the lanes fetch the whole history, and an obvious placeholder is not treated as a leaked secret
regression_test: check_repo_hygiene.py is run by five lanes
verification: the placeholder is still treated as a secret

symptom: the repair lane could never run, because there was nothing to read
root_cause: The repair lane was handed the failure log to diagnose, and it looked for it in a directory that nothing in this repository ever wrote, and for an artifact that no workflow ever uploaded. So it found nothing on every run, said so and gave up before it asked anything, and the repair-after-a-failed-generation capability had never existed.
evidence: there is no selfheal/ directory, nothing writes the two files it looked for, and the only artifacts uploaded are named paid-build and slingshot-installer
repro: run the repair lane and see that it finds no log
fix: the generate job keeps its output as an artifact, the workflow downloads it, and the repair lane looks in the places the log can land
regression_test: the lane's own log handling
verification: removing the new places makes the lane find nothing again

symptom: no build was ever steered by the community's vote
root_cause: The ballot was a weekly thing, opened on Monday and meant to steer the build on Friday, but it was only ever closed once it had aged out after twenty-one days. The Friday step was named 'Close this week's ballot' and ran the Monday job, which opens a ballot and refuses to open a second one. So the same ballot stayed open for three weeks, the build never saw a closed ballot, and the vote steered nothing.
evidence: the ballot lifetime is twenty-one days, the Friday step ran the Monday job, and vote_steer.py reads the winners of closed ballots
repro: run the Friday lane and look at whether the build was steered
fix: the ballot can be closed on demand, and the Friday lane closes it before the build reads the vote
regression_test: the weekly stage the Friday lane must run is checked by the audit
verification: removing the force close leaves the ballot open and the build unsteered

symptom: a corrupted state file took the daily lane down
root_cause: The lane's own state file was only checked at the top level, so a file holding a changes list instead of a table, or a list holding something that was not a record, made the cooldown check raise an AttributeError. A corrupted file took the lane down with a traceback instead of skipping the day, and the write was not atomic, so a crash mid-write left a truncated file that the next read took for an empty history.
evidence: a state file holding {"changes": {"a": 1}} raised an AttributeError in the cooldown check
repro: put each of those shapes in the daily lane's state file
fix: the shape is checked before it is used, and the write goes to a side file and is swapped in
regression_test: the lane's own state handling
verification: the old check crashes again

symptom: the pattern library taught every new app the paid bypass
root_cause: Every generated app inherits its patterns from PATTERNS.md, and that file still taught the query-string gate, months after the twenty-five apps that used it had been fixed. So a new app arrived with the bypass in it, and the free edition of a product that was on the store came back unlocked. The bad form is not shown in the library any more, because a library is what the model copies from, and the staging gate refuses an app whose limits come from the query string, so a model that learned it elsewhere cannot smuggle it back in.
evidence: the Friday lane's own log shows the app it generated was 5521 bytes with 'const PAID=new URLSearchParams(location.search).has(\'paid\')' in it, and the file it wrote to the site had the same line
repro: generate an app and look at how its edition is decided
fix: the library teaches the constant, the wrong form is not shown at all, and the gate refuses an app that does it anyway
regression_test: tier_gate_selftest.py checks the library does not teach the query-string gate, that it teaches the constant instead, and that the gate refuses an app that reads the edition from the URL
verification: putting the bad form back in the library makes the check fail

symptom: the builder overwrote a product that was on sale
root_cause: Every one of the forty-four concepts had been built, so the picker fell back to the whole list and regenerated one of them. The one it chose was a product that was on the store, and it overwrote the free edition of it with a fresh generation, which is the generation that carried the query-string gate. The customer was buying one edition and the other one was replaced underneath them. The lane has done this several times, and the history shows it: four candidate commits overwrote the same live app.
evidence: the Friday lane's log reads 'choosing from 44 unused concepts (built: 45)' and then 'concept: Offline password manager (password-manager)', and the candidate commit it made overwrote site/apps/password-manager-basic/app/index.html
repro: let every concept be built and ask what the picker returns
fix: the picker says there is nothing new to build and the lane treats that as a legitimate no-op week
regression_test: tier_gate_selftest.py checks that the picker never returns a product that is already on the site, and selftest_deep.py checks the same
verification: putting the fallback back makes both fail

symptom: the paid installer demanded admin and installed one folder deeper than it said
root_cause: The script installed to "$PROGRAMFILES64\<name>" but SetOutPath wrote into "$INSTDIR\<name>", so the directory page named one folder and the app landed one level below it, with every shortcut pointing at the deeper path. RequestExecutionLevel admin also put a UAC prompt in front of a $3 download, and Program Files is not writable, so a tool that saves beside its exe fails there.
evidence: dist/Offline password manager.nsi held InstallDir "$PROGRAMFILES64\Offline password manager" beside SetOutPath "$INSTDIR\Offline password manager" and RequestExecutionLevel admin.
repro: run build_installer_app on the paid app folder, read the generated .nsi
fix: Installs per user under %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\Slingshot Tools with RequestExecutionLevel user, writes into $INSTDIR itself, stores HKCU registry keys, and uninstalls the same folder.
regression_test: paidbuild_selftest.py refuses an admin prompt, a Program Files install folder, and a SetOutPath or shortcut that names the folder twice.
verification: Built the installer and ran it silently on this PC: exit 0 with no elevation prompt, files under %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\Slingshot Tools\Offline password manager, Start Menu and desktop shortcuts created, HKCU uninstall entry correct; the app launched, and uninstall.exe /S removed the folder, the shortcuts and the registry key.

symptom: every paid app opened as Slingshot Tool and checked for updates as an empty product
root_cause: The frozen launcher reads app/app.json for its window title, its update slug and the installed version, and no build step wrote one into the paid bundle. The title fell back to "Slingshot Tool", app_update.check was given slug "" so it only ever compared the company version, and the installed version always read 1.0.0.
evidence: the built bundle's app folder held index.html and icon.ico only, and the launched window's title was "Slingshot Tool"
repro: build a paid app, launch the exe, read the window title and app/app.json
fix: build_exe.write_meta writes app/app.json with the title, the catalogue slug from concept.json and a version, before PyInstaller copies the folder, and leaves a file the build already supplied alone.
regression_test: paidbuild_selftest.py checks the title, the catalogue slug rather than the dashed title, a version, and that an existing app.json is kept.
verification: rebuilt the password manager app and its installer: the installed window title is now "Offline password manager", the bundle carries {"title":"Offline password manager","slug":"password-manager","version":"1.0.0"}, and the app launched from the installed folder.

symptom: the site sold two products at $3.00 on a page that let anyone pay nothing
root_cause: The store project was created as a pay-what-you-want page with no minimum. The publish path proved the page answered and listed the file, but never checked that the page asked for the price the site advertised, so both live products were shown at $3.00 against a button that read "Download Now".
evidence: the public page carries Name your own price and a Download Now button, while site/apps.json lists password-manager and base64-tool at 3.0
repro: python -c "import itch_publish as ip; print(ip.price_is_asked('https://slingshot-tools.itch.io/slingshot-tools', 3.0))" prints False
fix: publish() reads the page's purchase block before advertising anything and refuses when the least a buyer can pay is below the advertised price, with the fix named in the log.
regression_test: itchpublish_selftest.py covers pay-what-you-want with and without a floor, a fixed price, a page that says Free, and a page with no readable price block.
verification: the check returns True for the three selling shapes and False for the live page, which is why the paid tier must not be re-advertised until the project's minimum price is set on itch.io
uncertainty: setting the minimum price is a manual step on itch.io; there is no API for it, so the gate can only refuse, not repair

symptom: verification published an app that had failed every repair round
root_cause: The tolerance branch only ran when fewer than 4000 tokens were left. With more allowance the code fell straight through to publish(), so a candidate that had failed every repair was published. The branch also judged the candidate on the scan taken before the repairs, not the last one, and it never looked at JavaScript errors at all.
evidence: the publish path was reached whenever tokenmeter.remaining(8000) >= 4000, with no check of the final repair result
repro: stage an app that qa_loop cannot repair, run verify_app with allowance left, and watch it publish
fix: The decision now reads the final repair round, refuses whenever allowance remains or any JS error survives, and only tolerates one dead control after the allowance is genuinely exhausted; a re-verified candidate also keeps its existing on-sale flag instead of silently hiding a live product.
regression_test: verifygate_selftest.py drives both branches and checks that publish is not reached after a failed repair, and that JS errors are never tolerated.
verification: the full suite passes and verify_app's publish condition reads only the last round and rejects JS errors

symptom: a JavaScript error was never repaired, so an app that looked finished did nothing
root_cause: When a scan found JS errors and no dead controls, the control list was empty, so the patcher was asked to patch zero controls, returned nothing, and the round ended without a single model call. Every syntax or runtime error survived all four rounds, and the app was then scanned again and reported with the same errors.
evidence: qa_loop's error branch set no work and continued; a scan with errors=['x'] and dead=[] produced no repair call
repro: generate an app with a syntax error, run qa_loop.repair_until_clean, and watch the error count never move
fix: An error-only scan now asks debug_team for one full-file correction, writes it to a trial file, rescans, and keeps it only when the error count fell and the dead controls did not rise.
regression_test: verifygate_selftest.py checks that the error-only path asks for a full-file repair; scan_selftest.py covers the scanner's result shape.
verification: the branch is exercised by the suite and the repair is discarded when a fresh scan disagrees

symptom: staging never rejected unusable model output, and published a paid edition with nothing to sell
root_cause: build_html_raw raises RuntimeError after its own retries, and stage_app did not catch it, so the rejection block that writes the NOT_VERIFIED event and the rejected script never ran. paid_features() was read before the escaping variant was chosen, so a doubly-escaped limit table looked like 'no paid features'. write_app's tier gate could also raise, which nothing caught, and an empty feature list was published with generic copy on both cards.
evidence: a run that produced no usable app printed a traceback and recorded no audit event; a run with no paid features still reached write_app
repro: feed stage_app a model reply that fails every variant, and one whose paid limits are escaped; the first crashes, the second sells nothing
fix: Every model call and write_app is wrapped, each rejection is audited and retried, the variant is chosen before the features are read, and an app with no paid features is rejected rather than published.
regression_test: tier_gate_selftest.py and variant_selftest.py cover the gate and the escape order; the release lane's audit trail now records each retry.
verification: both rejection paths return a retry instead of a traceback, and the suite is green

symptom: the scanner took the whole verify job down when the browser would not start

symptom: a no-op build republished an old candidate and rewrote a live product

symptom: the Windows runner decoded butler's output with the wrong code page

The upload had in fact succeeded: Batch file renamer-Setup.exe was listed on the page a minute later. The paid edition was left unsold and the release was marked incomplete.

repro: run itch_publish.py on a Windows runner with a real installer
fix: butler's output is captured as bytes and decoded with utf-8/replace, so no byte can abort the reader. The build check drops any earlier answer and retries for about a minute, because itch.io publishes a build asynchronously after butler returns.
regression_test: itchpublish_selftest.py checks the upload body has no text=True, that it decodes with replace, and that the publication check retries.
verification: the upload output is readable and the build is found on the page

repro: publish any third paid product, then run itchpublish_selftest.py
fix: The check derives its answer from data/itch.json, which is written only after the build is seen on the page and the price is charged, and publish_paid.py now records its products there too.
regression_test: itchpublish_selftest.py checks published tiers against the store state.

verification: a reader can find and store the cookie

symptom: a paid download introduced itself as the free edition
root_cause: Both editions are one generated file with the TIER constant flipped, but models write the edition into the footer as ordinary text. At least two products do: Batch file renamer's footer read 'RenameFlow (c) 2024 - Free basic edition' and coin-toss's pitched 'Free basic edition: quick flips ... Paid edition: ...'. Flipping TIER only changed the code, so the installer built by the real pipeline opened with 'Free basic edition' on the screen of someone who had just paid $3 for it. The repair lane had the same fault twice over: rebuild_paid reconstructed the paid file with _set_tier alone, so re-uploading a product would have reproduced the wrong footer even after this was fixed in write_app.

repro: install the paid installer and read the footer; then compare the free and paid copies of the same app
fix: make_app now decides an edition in one place, set_edition, used by write_app and by rebuild_paid. For the paid edition it renames a free-edition label to 'Full edition', drops a two-edition sales pitch back to just the paid half, and removes any sentence claiming the free edition's limits.
